title: Feature-level microbundle pricing experiments playbook
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Summary

This playbook describes the approach, experiment designs, measurement plan, and rollout steps for per-feature microbundle pricing experiments. The goal is to enable incremental monetization of discrete fidelity features (e.g., response-volatility-control, structured-output hooks, session-anchored embeddings) by offering tiny, composable bundles that developers can opt into. This document focuses on experiment hygiene, metric definitions, sample pricing matrices, simulation queries, and a safe rollout path for Hosted and Dedicated customers.

Background and motivation

- Problem: Many customers only need a small subset of high-cost fidelity features. Current tiered SKUs (e.g., Fidelity Bronze/Silver/Gold) are coarse and force overpayment or multiple product integrations.
- Hypothesis: Offering per-feature microbundles priced at sub-dollar-per-100k-token increments will increase revenue from low-volume customers and improve conversion from free trials without materially degrading unit economics or SLOs.
- Constraints: Pricing experiments must preserve existing customer SLAs and should be revenue-neutral in early A/B phases to avoid commercial disruption.

Objectives and success criteria

Primary objectives (OKR-aligned):
1) Achieve a 10–15% increase in ARPU among developer-tier customers who enable >=1 microbundle within 90 days of availability.
2) Maintain hosted inference 99.9% 95th-percentile token-latency baseline for customers enabling microbundles.
3) Demonstrate microbundle gross margin > 35% in simulation tests before GA.

Success metrics (measured per cohort):
- Adoption rate: percent of eligible customers who enable >=1 microbundle within 30 days.
- Incremental revenue: net new revenue attributable to microbundles (USD) measured monthly.
- Retention delta: 90-day retention difference between adopters and matched control.
- Cost delta: average per-token cost delta for adopters (runtime + infra amortized).
- SLA impact: change in 95th p50/p95 token latency, OOM/eviction rates for impacted pools.

Microbundle taxonomy (examples)

- Low-cost feature microbundles (target price $0.20–$2 / 100k tokens):
  - Structured-output hook (JSON schema enforcement)
  - Soft-stop hallucination penalty (lightweight reranker)
  - Small-session pinned embeddings (per-session retention 1–2 keys)

- Medium-cost microbundles (target price $2–$10 / 100k tokens):
  - Deterministic sampling / constrained decoding primitives
  - Enhanced KV-cache persistence (session-hardened warm cache)

- High-cost microbundles (target price $10–$50 / 100k tokens):
  - Response-volatility-control (heavy reranker + cross-attention adapters)
  - Multimodal-attachment-fusion (extra compute for small images/metadata)

Experiment designs

1) Pricing A/B (Revenue-neutral pricing test)
- Setup: Randomly assign new developer signups to control (no microbundles; existing tiers) or experiment (see microbundle opt-in modal). For the experiment cohort, show suggested microbundles with prices and a free 14-day trial credit for the first microbundle.
- Sample size: minimum 1,200 signups per arm to detect a 7% ARPU lift with 80% power.
- Duration: 90 days.
- Measurement: tracking of adoption rate, incremental revenue, and retention delta.

2) Feature-only opt-in (Product-led adoption)
- Setup: Enable microbundle toggle in Console -> Developer Sandbox. No forced price shown for first 30 days; instead show a consumption quota limit and notification of impending charge.
- Duration: pilot 30–60 days.
- Measurement: friction-to-adopt (time-to-first-use), conversion to paid after quota.

3) Price elasticity ladder (staged price exposure)
- Setup: For experiment cohort, randomly assign one of three suggested price points per microbundle (low/medium/high).
- Measurement: discrete demand curve per feature; track marginal adoption drop per 10% price increase.

Measurement plan and instrumentation

Required telemetry and events:
- event.microbundle.shown (user_id, signup_cohort, bundle_id, suggested_price, ui_context)
- event.microbundle.enrolled (user_id, bundle_id, start_ts, trial_end_ts, pricing_tier)
- event.microbundle.usage (user_id, bundle_id, tokens_consumed, model_variant, runtime_pool)
- metric.runtime.cost_per_token (by model_variant, pool, minute)
- metric.latency.p95_tokens (by customer_id, route, model_variant)

Suggested SQL queries (example)

1) Adoption rate by cohort (Postgres-like):
SELECT cohort, bundle_id, COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) AS adopters, SUM(tokens_consumed) AS tokens
FROM microbundle_events
WHERE event_date BETWEEN '2026-12-01' AND '2027-01-10'
GROUP BY cohort, bundle_id;

2) Incremental revenue estimate (simple model):
-- assumes price USD per 100k tokens, prorated by tokens_consumed
SELECT cohort, bundle_id, SUM(tokens_consumed) AS tokens,
       SUM((tokens_consumed/100000.0) * price_per_100k) AS revenue_estimate
FROM microbundle_usage JOIN microbundle_catalog USING (bundle_id)
GROUP BY cohort, bundle_id;

Cost simulation steps

1) For each bundle, compute worst-case per-token cost: runtime + infra overhead + routing credit.
2) Simulate 95th percentile session retention impact (KV cache warmup) using existing workload traces (use the simulation harness from eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite).
3) Run Monte Carlo on adoption percentiles (5/25/50/75/95) to estimate margin sensitivity.

Sample pricing matrix (illustrative)

| bundle_id | short_desc                        | price/100k | expected_cost/100k | margin_est | notes |
|-----------|-----------------------------------|------------|--------------------|------------|-------|
| B-JSON1   | Structured-output (light)         | $1.50      | $0.70              | 53%        | low CPU, small cost delta |
| B-KV1     | Session pinned embeddings (small) | $2.50      | $1.20              | 52%        | increases memory usage per session |
| B-RER1    | Soft reranker (light)             | $5.00      | $3.20              | 36%        | higher CPU; monitor p95 latency |

Customer-facing UX patterns

- Console: "Add microbundle" flow inside route and project settings. Display estimated incremental cost per 10k tokens and projected monthly spend given last 30-day usage.
- API: Allow billing_action="enable_microbundle" on per-route creation. Document the feature in SDKs with example JSON payload: 

{
  "route": "/chat",
  "microbundles": ["B-JSON1", "B-KV1"]
}

- Usage billing: Microbundles appear as separate line items in Billing -> Usage with a descriptive label and cost-per-usage.

Safeguards and guardrails

- Default caps: Any newly-enabled microbundle defaults to a 30-day usage cap of $5 for free-trial cohorts. Admins can raise caps.
- SLA isolation: Microbundle-enabled traffic is routed to dedicated soft pools tagged with "microbundle-experiment" to avoid cross-tenant P95 regressions.
- Automated rollback thresholds: If any of the following occur during experiment window, pause new enrollments and trigger review:
  - p95 latency increase > 20% vs baseline for experiment cohort
  - error rate (5xx) delta > 0.5% absolute
  - infra cost per-token unexpectedly increases > 30% vs simulated estimate

Rollout and lifecycle plan

1) Internal alpha (0–4 weeks): small developer pilot (10 customers). Validate instrumentation and billing events. Owners: Product (Ava), Eng Runtime (Ethan), Billing (Priya).
2) Beta experiment (4–12 weeks): A/B pricing ladder and feature-only opt-in across new signups. Minimum sample size rules apply.
3) Analyze results and tune prices (weeks 12–16): compute elasticity and run margin sims.
4) Gradual GA (weeks 16–28): enable in Console, create migration guide for existing customers, add UI education. Offer opt-out windows for Dedicated customers.

Owners and responsibilities

- Product (owner): Ava Martinez — experiment design, success criteria, go/no-go.
- Eng Runtime: Ethan Kim — routing, pool tagging, p95 monitoring.
- Billing & Revenue Ops: Priya Patel — usage line-itemization, invoices, revenue measurement.
- Analytics: Jordan Lee — experiment instrumentation, cohort analysis, SQL queries.
- Legal & Compliance: review pricing language and contracts pre-GA.

FAQ and open decisions

- Q: Should microbundles be available to Dedicated customers at GA?
  - A: Dedicated customers require contract amendments. Default GA will be Hosted only; Dedicated enablement will be opt-in via sales playbook.

- Q: How do we prevent abuse (e.g., switch between cheap microbundles to exploit fallback)?
  - A: Enforce per-route entitlement and minimum billing period per bundle (30 days). Track abusive patterns and escalate to SRE/Trust.

Appendix: example rollout checklist (numbered)

1. Verify telemetry is live for event.microbundle.* (Analytics sign-off).
2. Deploy UI modal with A/B assignment flags (DevEx sign-off).
3. Provision microbundle routing pools with isolation tags (Eng Runtime).
4. Set trial credit caps and billing line-item templates (Billing Ops).
5. Run initial 10-customer alpha for 2 weeks and collect p95/5xx metrics.
6. Proceed to Beta only if SLA regressions are within thresholds.
